title: The Hottest Question for CEOs Right Now
author: Joel Trammell
summary: Joel Trammell, a longtime CEO, says the hottest question among chief executives is "What is your AI strategy?" and that he answers it with another: "What is your people strategy?" His argument is that AI is not software, which is a tool, but a new way to access intelligence, so the real question is how a company already puts intelligence to work, which is its management system. AI therefore amplifies whatever system exists, and he cites a 2025 Harvard study correlating skill at leading AI agents with skill at leading human teams. He offers six diagnostic questions on strategy clarity, talent, ownership, coaching, information and cross-department coordination. A fictional CEO, Jack, rolls out agents on top of departments already at cross-purposes and simply gets confusion at machine speed. The remedy is a companywide operating system that makes mission, values, decision rights and review rhythms explicit enough for both people and AI.
points: AI amplifies the management system a company already has, so weak management is accelerated rather than fixed.
Skill at managing people predicts skill at managing AI agents, according to a 2025 Harvard study with a 0.81 correlation.
Six questions test readiness: strategy, right people, ownership, coaching, available information and cross-department coordination.
Coordination costs grow fast with each participant, so adding agents multiplies unresolved conflicts into a network of expensive confusion.
A simple, explicit operating system gives employees and agents the shared context to decide which opportunities are worth pursuing.
quotes: It sounds like a smart question, but I answered it with another one. What is your people strategy? I wasn’t changing the subject. I was asking the question that I think comes before any answer to “AI strategy” is possible.
AI is a different beast. It is a new way to get access to intelligence. Until now, the only way a company could get intelligence was to hire people.
AI amplifies whatever management system already exists. Without one, it accelerates work in the wrong direction.

Before you draw up a plan to deploy hundreds more AI agents into your company, consider how well you’re managing the hundreds of intelligent human beings already working there. Do they understand what they’re supposed to accomplish? Are they getting the direction, information and coaching they need? If your organization struggles to make effective use of human intelligence, introducing artificial intelligence will hardly solve the problem.
The departments were already working at cross-purposes. Now they’re doing it at machine speed.

Coordination gets harder with each new participant. Ten people have 45 possible one-to-one relationships; a hundred have 4,950. Add agents across departments, and unresolved conflicts become an ever-larger network of expensive confusion.

A company has to know what it stands for and where it is going, even when the CEO isn’t physically present. Otherwise every smart employee, and every AI agent, is left to invent those answers from whatever instructions happen to be closest.
